articleTitle: A mutual alternative routing model for circuit-switched networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Making Life Easier - Network Design and Management Tools (Digest No: 1996/217)
abstract: Security measures are being applied in the Telecom Eireann trunk telephone network to minimise disruption due to excess traffic or system failure. Dynamic measures, such as network management, will be deployed in the very near future, but in the meantime, static measures are being applied, Geographically separate exchanges of the same status are provided at major nodes with traffic shared equally between them on separate transmission links. Rerouting is provided automatically when a system fails, but at a reduced grade of service. This paper presents a model which simulates this concept of mutual alternative routing using the UNIX-based OPNET package.

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Making Life Easier - Network Design and Management Tools (Digest No: 1996/217)
abstract: It is a fact that the UK telecommunications market is becoming more and more complex. This complexity, particularly in the interconnect/regulatory and marketing areas poses a growing challenge to the switched network design and planning engineer. Before starting to think about planning the future it is essential to understand current calling behaviour. Some information about calling patterns is available from standard statistics generated by telephone exchanges, but this tends to be limited to high level counters at a route or cell level. Fortunately there is a much more detailed source of information about calling patterns. This is produced from almost all types of switch as the call record used for billing purposes. This paper describes some simple but powerful software tools and methods which have been used for manipulating and summarising this low level data to provide a whole range of useful results.

abstract: The timely deployment of a reliable telephony network depends on careful planning, critical decisions, and efficient communication between several disciplines long before the first access to the network is ever made. This article considers some of these decisions and how a comprehensive software tool can play an important role in the design and maintenance of the network.

articleTitle: Making life easier-network design and management tools
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Making Life Easier - Network Design and Management Tools (Digest No: 1996/217)
abstract: A number of entrepreneurial companies, in the mid 80s and early 90s, rose to the challenge of producing the software tools and expert services for cellular operators worldwide. Of these, Mobile Systems International (MSI) and it's PlaNET product range have become the quality market leader. The authors look at the history of planning tools and categorise them into different generations of tools by looking at the level of overall focus the tools give of the system.

articleTitle: Automatic call generation and analysis-network testing and cellular survey tools
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Making Life Easier - Network Design and Management Tools (Digest No: 1996/217)
abstract: There is a growing need for cellular network performance surveys in an increasingly competitive cellular phone environment. New operators are under great pressure from their share holders to bring their network up for commercial service but at the same time they do not want to compromise their service quality. For existing operators, the drive is to achieve optimum spectral efficiency for the growing traffic demand in their preciously allocated spectral band. The motivation is threefold, (1) to quantify network performance and operating parameters, (2) to investigate specific network problems, and (3) to optimise the network. The Surveyor is designed to enable engineers to perform field surveys in these areas with ease. It is a proven system helping operators over the world to capture and analyse cellular data which enables engineers to constantly monitor, improve, and refine a cellular mobile network's quality of service. The Surveyor is an advanced continuous (or carrier) wave (CW) and handset survey system which features full handset message decoding in real-time for up to eight or more handsets of the same or different types. It can interface to practically any Global Positioning System (GPS) navigation system and also supports other navigation systems.

articleTitle: Managing changes in a complex world
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Making Life Easier - Network Design and Management Tools (Digest No: 1996/217)
abstract: The telecommunications industry is characterised by enormous complexity and rapid change. In this environment, competitive advantage goes to companies that can plan and manage changes to their operations and infrastructure most effectively. BT has developed an in-house system called TRIADS (Telecoms Requirements, Impact Analysis and Decision Support) to address this need. The primary role of TRIADS is to facilitate high-level design and migration planning for BT's operational support systems (OSS) infrastructure. The scale and complexity of this infrastructure, consisting of more than a thousand interconnected computer systems, provides a considerable challenge for the planner. In planning a change he must consider not only the effects on other systems, but also the impact on supported products and services, business processes and corporate data usage. Furthermore, it essential that each planner understands the context of his proposals in relation to other planned changes to the infrastructure. TRIADS addresses these needs by modelling all the relevant business dimensions and providing a powerful front-end application to view and edit the model from multiple, customised viewpoints. It incorporates a sophisticated data management scheme which enables data to be dynamically maintained on-line and facilitates group-working across different sectors of the business. The application adds significant value to the data by providing a range of facilities for navigation, information processing and impact analysis, together with electronic tool support for the migration planning process.

abstract: This discussion is focused around the relationship that a marketing and engineering group of a mobile telephony operator should work towards. This work specifically details how software tools are now available to help marketing provide the necessary inputs to the engineering groups for the design and build of mobile telephone networks.

articleTitle: Optimising performance of the network-network generated statistics
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Making Life Easier - Network Design and Management Tools (Digest No: 1996/217)
abstract: This paper outlines how network generated performance statistics can be used in the engineering process of optimising a network design, as well as being a vital part of the operational process of maintaining quality of service given an existing network design. The characteristics of performance management tools that can help an administration in these processes are considered.
